title: Entitlements-to-Purchase, Travel, and Change: Operating Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook documents standard company-wide procedures for entitlements (access & permissions), change management, procurement and expenses, vendor onboarding, and travel expense handling. It is intended for requesters, approvers, finance partners, IT, and security teams. Follow the step-by-step flows below; exceptions must be approved by Finance-Legal and Security.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and long-term vendors.
- Covers: account and resource access requests, privileged access lifecycle, infrastructure and product change requests, purchase approvals and expense reimbursements, vendor evaluation & onboarding, and employee travel expenses.

Roles & responsibilities

- Requester: initiates requests and provides required justification, cost center, and supporting docs.
- Approver: manager-level approver for role/access/purchase; for purchases > $25k, involve Budget Owner (Director+) and Procurement.
- Finance: validates budgets, issues PO or expense reimbursement.
- Security/IT: reviews access risk, approves privileged access, configures IAM and SSO rules.
- Vendor Management Owner: owns contracts, risk reviews, and onboarding checklist.
- Change Manager: reviews high-risk infra/product changes and coordinates rollouts.

Access & permissions lifecycle

Principles

1. Least privilege by default.
2. Temporary elevation for time-bound tasks with automatic expiry.
3. Role-based groups for common duties; ad-hoc permissions require justification.

Standard request flow (self-service where possible)

1. Requester opens an Access Request ticket via the Access Portal (internal app) and selects the target resource (e.g., GCP project, Kubernetes namespace, Redwood Console route).
2. Attach clear justification and estimated duration.
3. Manager approval is required for any new entitlement. For privileged grants (Sudo, DB write, production deploy), Security must co-approve.
4. IT implements the change and sets an expiry timestamp.
5. Automated audit records are generated; requester gets a confirmation email with expiry.

Temporary elevation (Emergency & Scheduled)

- Emergency: Owner oncall/time-window approval + post-hoc review within 48 hours.
- Scheduled: Use the Temporary Access template and set auto-revoke; Security performs risk assessment for >72h privileges.

Access review cadence and metrics

- Quarterly entitlement reviews per team; team leads must attest to current members and orphaned accounts.
- KPI: 100% of privileged grants with auto-expiry; target 95% quarterly completion of access reviews.

Change management (product & infra)

Risk classes

- Low: Documentation, non-production config updates.
- Medium: Back-end config changes with no customer impact.
- High: Database migrations, production traffic routing, changes affecting SLA.

Submission checklist

| Item | Required? | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Change request form (JIRA) | Yes | Requester | Include rollback plan |
| Impact analysis | Yes for Medium/High | Requester/Eng Lead | List services & SLOs impacted |
| Security review | Yes for High | Security | Include threat surface & secrets plan |
| Stakeholder signoff | Yes for Medium/High | Product/Support/Frontend | Email threads or signoff field |

Approval and scheduling

1. Create a Change ticket in the Change board and tag the Change Manager.
2. For High risk, schedule a Change Advisory Board (CAB) review; CAB meets daily for high-frequency environments and weekly otherwise.
3. Minimum 72-hour lead for High risk changes; 24-hour lead for Medium.
4. Runbook & rollback steps must be attached before deployment.

Post-change verification

- Run smoke tests and synthetic checks as defined in the runbook.
- Incident window monitoring for 2x the change duration.
- Change Manager marks the ticket as complete only after verification.

Procurement & expenses (purchases, POs, reimbursements)

Spending tiers and approval matrix

- Tier A: <= $2,000 — Manager approval.
- Tier B: $2,001–$25,000 — Manager + Budget Owner.
- Tier C: > $25,000 — Manager + Budget Owner + Procurement & Legal review.

Purchasing flow (standard indirect procurement)

1. Requester fills the Purchase Request form (fields: vendor, description, business justification, GL code, cost center, estimated total).
2. Manager approves in the procurement tool.
3. Finance validates budget and issues a PO for Tier B/C.
4. Vendor receives PO; procurement owner routes contract for signature if required.

Expense reimbursement (travel & non-travel)

- Employees submit expenses within 30 days of incurrence. Attach receipts for any single item > $25.
- Per-diem rules follow the Travel section below.
- Corporate card transactions must include business purpose and attendee list if >$150.

Vendor onboarding & contract checklist

Vendor categorization

- Low risk: SaaS with no access to customer data (e.g., analytics dashboards).
- Medium risk: Vendors processing internal data or integrated systems.
- High risk: Vendors handling customer PII, infrastructure, or privileged access.

Onboarding steps (minimum)

1. Vendor Risk Assessment: Procurement triggers a questionnaire; Security scores risk (scale 0–100).
2. Legal approves contract terms (data processing addendum, indemnification, breach notification timelines).
3. InfoSec completes a security checklist (MFA, encryption at rest, SOC2/ISO attestation if required).
4. Create a least-privilege service account or API key; define rotation cadence (default: 90 days).
5. Define SLAs, monitoring hooks, and escalation contacts in the vendor record.

Contract templates & retention

- Use the canonical Vendor Agreement and Data Processing Agreement templates stored in the Procurement library.
- Contracts are retained and indexed in the Contract Repository for the contract lifetime + 7 years.

Travel policy & expense rules (summary)

Principles

- Prefer cost-effective travel that meets business needs.
- Bookings should use the corporate travel tool where possible to unlock negotiated rates.

Booking & approvals

1. Create a Travel Request that includes purpose, itinerary, estimated cost, and approver.
2. Manager approves trips > $1,000 in estimated total.

Per-diem and meals

- Domestic: $75/day (covers meals & incidentals) — receipts not required within per-diem.
- International: country-specific per-diem published in the Travel Rates table in the appendix.

Airfare & lodging

- Economy or basic economy for trips < 6 hours one-way; premium economy or business must be justified and pre-approved.
- Lodging: reasonable/standard room at hotels on the corporate preferred list.

Expense submission example (CLI)

- Submit via expenses UI or using our expense CLI:

  redwood-expense submit --trip-id TRIP-2025-43 --receipt ./receipt.pdf --amount 465.12 --category lodging

Templates, forms, and attachments

Included template names (in the Templates library)

- "Temporary-Access-Request-template.md"
- "Change-Request-runbook-template.md"
- "Purchase-Request-form.csv"
- "Vendor-onboarding-checklist.xlsx"
- "Travel-Request-form.md"

Escalation matrix and SLAs

- Finance turnaround for approvals: Tier A — 24 hours, Tier B — 3 business days, Tier C — 10 business days.
- Security review for privileged access: standard review within 48 hours, expedited for critical operations within 4 hours.

Audit & compliance

- Audit logs: all entitlements and change approvals are logged in the central AuditLedger service and retained for minimum 2 years.
- Quarterly internal audits: Procurement and Security will produce a cross-functional audit report to the Exec Risk Committee.

Exceptions and emergency carve-outs

- Exception requests must be logged and include compensating controls, approval from Finance-Legal and Security, and an explicit expiration date.
- Emergency procurements (e.g., critical burst capacity) require post-facto approvals within 72 hours.

Appendix: Quick reference tables

| Approval Type | Approver | SLA | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Access (standard) | Manager | 48h | Auto-expiry recommended |
| Privileged Access | Manager + Security | 48h | Must include audit hooks |
| Purchase <= $2k | Manager | 24h | Fast track via corporate card |
| Purchase > $25k | Procurement + Legal | 10bd | Requires PO and contract |
